subject: Renewal discussion: Lattice Health capacity uplift and bake-off contingency
messages:
From: Alex Porter <ap@latticehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@latticehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — capacity uplift and upcoming vendor bake-off

Hi Stephanie / Karthik,

Quick heads-up from our side: our platform team has flagged that starting Jan we expect a ~2.5x peak token throughput across several pipelines. The execs have also requested we run a side-by-side bake-off for inference cost and latency across three vendors as part of the renewal evaluation.

We like Redwood's latency profile, but procurement is pushing for stronger TCO evidence and a clear migration cost baseline should we decide to move. Can Redwood provide the following by next Thursday (9/23)?
- A short benchmark report showing p95 latency at our projected p99 concurrency, with the current model and a 1.5x and 2.5x input length profile.
- An estimate for the monthly incremental cost at +2.5x tokens and recommended configuration (batching/quant) to control spend.
- A draft amendment clarifying committed capacity and an escape clause that keeps data residency and audit logging intact.

If you can also join a 30-min call with our infra and procurement on Friday that helps.

Thanks —
Alex Porter
Head of Platform, Lattice Health
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <ap@latticehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity uplift and upcoming vendor bake-off

Alex —

Appreciate the context. We'll own the benchmark and the commercial draft; high level plan below. I'll book the Friday slot (30 min) and loop in the right folks from our performance team.

Planned deliverables by Thu 9/23 EOD PST:
- "redwood-benchmark-v2.pdf": p50/p95/p99 numbers for current model across concurrency profiles and sequence lengths (we'll include both hosted and a dedicated-optimized run).
- A cost delta table with recommended runtime config (suggested batching window + quantization level) and estimated monthly spend at +2.5x tokens.
- "redwood-draft-amendment.docx": proposed contract language for committed capacity adjustments, data residency, retention, and a clear remediation SLA for performance regressions.

For the Friday call, proposed attendees: me (renewal lead), Karthik (solutions + perf), Marissa (CS lead for rollout), and Ben (pricing). Expect a short demo of the benchmark artifacts and a 10-minute Q&A.

A couple of asks for you to speed things up: can you share the production p95/p99 tail logs for the last 30 days (or a sampling) and an exported token distribution CSV? That will let us mirror your traffic mix instead of synthetic profiles.

I'll follow with calendar invite.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Porter <ap@latticehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@latticehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity uplift and upcoming vendor bake-off

Stephanie — thanks, and quick update: procurement would like the benchmark to include a 3rd-party cold-start test (to measure caching behavior after short downtimes) and an explicit failover run that demonstrates degraded-mode latency for a 10% capacity loss.

Attached: token-distribution-sep.csv (sent separately by our infra lead). Friday's window is 11:00–11:30 PT — procurement is firm on time.

We also attached our standard commercial playbook — procurement will want the amendment to map to their SOW template.

Best,
Alex
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <ap@latticehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity uplift and upcoming vendor bake-off

Alex / procurement —

Thanks for the data. We completed the run and uploaded artifacts: redwood-benchmark-v2.pdf (includes cold-start profiles and a 10%-degraded failover simulation), and a short one-page executive summary. Key takeaways:
- p95 latency (hosted) at projected peak concurrency: 210 ms (current model), p99: 480 ms.
- Dedicated-optimized runtime with light quantization reduces p95 to 160 ms and p99 to 350 ms at the same token load.
- At +2.5x token usage, recommended configuration (dedicated pool, 8s batching window, L4 quant) yields estimated incremental monthly cost of $36k (vs $92k if left unoptimized).

Attached is redwood-draft-amendment.docx with language for: capacity bands, rollback / canary windows, data residency confirmation, and a remediation credit schedule tied to p95 SLO breaches. I highlighted two clauses procurement historically asks to adjust (termination for convenience notice period & audit window length).

Proposed next steps (short):
1) 30-min call now (on the invite) to walk top-line numbers and answer procurement questions.
2) After alignment, we push a tracked-draft into DocuSign for review and (if acceptable) a 2-week signature window.
3) If procurement insists on a bake-off pilot with a competing vendor, we propose a constrained PoC where Redwood provides an independent, side-by-side run (same input traces) and we commit to a commercial bridge if metrics fall within 10% of their incumbent for p95 and cost.

If procurement asks for further concessions on price we can discuss a short-term capacity credit in exchange for a 12-month committed uplift. Ben, can you prepare a single-slide concession matrix for today's call? Karthik, please keep the one-page executive summary ready for the C-suite.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments referenced: redwood-benchmark-v2.pdf (report), redwood-draft-amendment.docx (commercial amendment)
